sim.title: Survive the month
sim.intro: This is your pocket money for the month. Make five choices and see what is left.
sim.assumptions: Example prices. A practice month, not advice.
sim.xpOnce: XP counts on your first run each day.
sim.recharge.title: Your phone plan runs out. You need it for class groups and homework.
sim.recharge.lesson0: It covers everything, but costs ₹100 more than you need.
sim.recharge.lesson1: Data covers class groups and homework. Paying only for what you use saves ₹100.
sim.recharge.lesson2: No plan means missed class updates. This was a need.
sim.bus.title: You need to get to college every day this month.
sim.bus.lesson0: One pass for the month costs ₹200 less than daily tickets.
sim.bus.lesson1: 20 days × ₹40 = ₹800, which is ₹200 more than the pass.
sim.bus.lesson2: Rides aren't always there, and you may miss class. Travel was a need.
sim.outing.title: Friends plan a movie and food on Saturday.
sim.outing.lesson0: Fun, but a want: ₹500 is a sixth of your month's money.
sim.outing.lesson1: You still see your friends and keep ₹350.
sim.outing.lesson2: Skipping a want once keeps ₹500 for later needs.
sim.examFee.title: Surprise! A ₹700 exam fee is due this week.
sim.examFee.lesson0: Paying on time avoids the fine. Money kept aside handles surprises.
sim.examFee.lesson1: The ₹100 fine buys nothing. Surprises are why we keep a buffer.
sim.examFee.lesson2: Missing an exam fee can cost you the exam. This was a need.
sim.sneakers.title: Sneakers you like are on sale.
sim.sneakers.lesson0: A sale is still spending. Check what is left for the month first.
sim.sneakers.lesson1: Half the price, and the money left can start your savings.
sim.sneakers.lesson2: Money left at the end of the month can go into savings.

sims.grow-savings.title: Grow your savings
sims.grow-savings.intro: You can put aside ₹500 a month from pocket money. Make four choices and see how time and interest change what it becomes.
sims.grow-savings.assumptions: Assumes an example 7% a year, the same every year, and no tax. Real rates change. An illustration, not a promise or advice.
sims.grow-savings.where.title: Where does your ₹500 a month go for the next 10 years?
sims.grow-savings.where.1: An account that pays simple interest
sims.grow-savings.where.2: An account that pays compound interest
sims.grow-savings.where.lesson0: After 10 years you have exactly what you put in: ₹60,000. Meanwhile prices have risen, so it buys less.
sims.grow-savings.where.lesson1: Simple interest pays only on what you put in. It grows, but slower than compound interest at the same rate.
sims.grow-savings.where.lesson2: Compound interest also pays interest on earlier interest. At the example 7%, ₹60,000 put in becomes about ₹86,500.
sims.grow-savings.start.title: When do you start?
sims.grow-savings.start.2: Someday, when I have more money
sims.grow-savings.start.lesson0: Time does most of the work. Ten years at the example rate gives about ₹86,500.
sims.grow-savings.start.lesson1: Starting 5 years later leaves 5 years to grow: about ₹35,800 instead of ₹86,500 at the same date.
sims.grow-savings.start.lesson2: "Someday" often never comes. A small amount started early can beat a bigger amount started late.
sims.grow-savings.dip.title: Three years in, a new phone tempts you. Your old one still works.
sims.grow-savings.dip.0: Take out everything and buy it
sims.grow-savings.dip.2: Leave it and save separately for the phone
sims.grow-savings.dip.lesson0: You start again from zero and lose the years the money had already grown.
sims.grow-savings.dip.lesson1: Half keeps growing, but the half you took out stops earning interest for good.
sims.grow-savings.dip.lesson2: A separate goal for the phone keeps your long-term money growing untouched.
sims.grow-savings.raise.title: Your pocket money goes up by ₹500 a month.
sims.grow-savings.raise.lesson0: Steady saving still works. Raising it when income rises would grow it faster.
sims.grow-savings.raise.lesson1: At the example rate, ₹1,000 a month for 10 years becomes about ₹1,73,000. Saving more when you get more is the easiest raise.
sims.grow-savings.raise.lesson2: What you saved keeps earning, but nothing new is added, so growth slows a lot.
sims.spot-the-scam.title: Spot the scam
sims.spot-the-scam.intro: Four messages reach your phone today. Decide what to do with each one.
sims.spot-the-scam.assumptions: Made-up messages based on common scams. Real ones can look different. When unsure, ask a trusted adult.
sims.spot-the-scam.otp.title: A caller says: "I'm from your bank. Your account will be blocked. Tell me the OTP you just got."
sims.spot-the-scam.otp.1: Hang up and call the number on the bank's card or app
sims.spot-the-scam.otp.lesson0: An OTP approves a payment. Banks never ask for it. Sharing it can empty the account.
sims.spot-the-scam.otp.lesson1: You checked through a number you found yourself, not one the caller gave. That settles whether anything is wrong.
sims.spot-the-scam.otp.lesson2: Not sharing was right. Checking with the bank yourself, and reporting the call, is safer still.
sims.spot-the-scam.loan.title: An ad says: "Instant loan in 5 minutes! No documents. Install our app and pay a ₹499 fee first."
sims.spot-the-scam.loan.0: Install it and pay the fee
sims.spot-the-scam.loan.lesson0: A fee before a loan is a classic sign of a fake loan app. The fee is gone and the loan never comes.
sims.spot-the-scam.loan.lesson1: Such apps often ask for your contacts and photos, then use them to threaten people. Looking isn't free.
sims.spot-the-scam.loan.lesson2: Urgency, no checks and pay-first are three warning signs together. Real lenders check documents.
sims.spot-the-scam.scheme.title: A senior says: "Put in ₹2,000, bring 3 friends, and it doubles in a month. Guaranteed!"
sims.spot-the-scam.scheme.0: Say no and tell a trusted adult
sims.spot-the-scam.scheme.2: Put in only ₹500 to test it
sims.spot-the-scam.scheme.lesson0: Guaranteed doubling plus "bring friends" is how Ponzi schemes work: early members are paid with new members' money until it collapses.
sims.spot-the-scam.scheme.lesson1: You could lose your money and your friends' money. Nothing honest guarantees doubling in a month.
sims.spot-the-scam.scheme.lesson2: Such schemes often pay small amounts at first to win trust. A small test can pull you in deeper.
sims.spot-the-scam.alert.title: An SMS from your bank's usual sender name: "₹250 paid from your account at a shop." No link. You didn't shop today.
sims.spot-the-scam.alert.1: Check my balance in the bank's own app and tell the bank if it's not mine
sims.spot-the-scam.alert.2: Search online for a helpline number and call the first result
sims.spot-the-scam.alert.lesson0: Not every message is a scam. A real alert for a payment you didn't make needs action quickly.
sims.spot-the-scam.alert.lesson1: You verified in the official app and reported fast. Quick reports give the best chance of getting money back.
sims.spot-the-scam.alert.lesson2: Scammers post fake helpline numbers online. Use the number on your card or in the bank's app.
sims.emi-or-save.title: EMI or save first?
sims.emi-or-save.intro: A ₹15,000 phone is on offer. Make four choices and see what each way of buying really costs.
sims.emi-or-save.assumptions: Example prices, an example 18% a year EMI rate and example fees. Real offers differ. An illustration, not advice.
sims.emi-or-save.how.title: How do you get the ₹15,000 phone?
sims.emi-or-save.how.2: Save ₹1,250 a month for 12 months, then buy
sims.emi-or-save.how.lesson0: About ₹1,375 a month, ₹16,500 in total: roughly ₹1,500 extra for having it now.
sims.emi-or-save.how.lesson1: ₹15,000 + ₹1,500 fee = ₹16,500. "No-cost" can still cost: always add fees to the total.
sims.emi-or-save.how.lesson2: You pay ₹15,000, nothing extra, and owe nobody. The cost is waiting a year.
sims.emi-or-save.need.title: Your current phone is slow but works. What now?
sims.emi-or-save.need.0: Buy now, everyone has a new one
sims.emi-or-save.need.1: Fix it for ₹1,500 and keep saving
sims.emi-or-save.need.2: Borrow the money from a friend
sims.emi-or-save.need.lesson0: This is a want, not a need. Buying because others did is how budgets break.
sims.emi-or-save.need.lesson1: A small repair buys time, and the saving plan stays on track.
sims.emi-or-save.need.lesson2: It is still a loan. Money owed to friends can cost the friendship if you can't repay on time.
sims.emi-or-save.short.title: Your cousin has a phone on EMI and is ₹1,000 short this month. What should he do?
sims.emi-or-save.short.1: Cut wants this month and pay on time
sims.emi-or-save.short.2: Take a quick app loan to pay it
sims.emi-or-save.short.lesson0: A missed EMI brings a late fee and a mark on his credit record, which makes later loans harder.
sims.emi-or-save.short.lesson1: An EMI is a fixed bill: it comes before wants. One tight month costs less than a late fee.
sims.emi-or-save.short.lesson2: A loan to repay a loan adds a second interest bill. That is how debt piles up.
sims.emi-or-save.upsell.title: The shop says: "Take the ₹25,000 model for just ₹900 more a month!"
sims.emi-or-save.upsell.1: Ask the salesperson which is best
sims.emi-or-save.upsell.2: Work out the total cost first
sims.emi-or-save.upsell.lesson0: ₹900 × 12 = ₹10,800 more. A small monthly number can hide a big total.
sims.emi-or-save.upsell.lesson1: The salesperson earns from selling more. Ask, but do the sums yourself.
sims.emi-or-save.upsell.lesson2: Total cost, not the monthly amount, tells you what you really pay. If you couldn't afford it twice, think again.
